RBI Acts to Absorb Record Liquidity Surge in Banking System

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is undertaking measures to absorb a significant surge of liquidity in the Indian banking system, which has been exacerbated by record diaspora inflows. The banking system is awash with surplus liquidity, reportedly reaching ₹7 lakh crore and potentially exceeding ₹15 lakh crore. To address this, the RBI announced a 30-day variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) auction for September 7 to withdraw ₹7 lakh crore. Additionally, the RBI is tapping longer-duration reverse repos and considering a potential interest rate hike in October, as call money rates have fallen below the policy repo rate. These actions aim to manage liquidity and potentially control inflation.
